correctness.rationale: The exact variational interpolant is reconstructed on arbitrary circular gaps, yielding w_i=t_i-a_i c_gamma and a single scalar crossing. Two doubled gaps give T=h^2+12h^3. Local integration gives the four minimal hat ratios (7/9)pi^2 h+O(h^3); every other retained-node ratio is at least 2pi^2 h+O(h^3). Bubble integration gives B=h^2/6+O(h^4); quotient expansion gives Gamma=(7/3)N+49pi^2/27+O(1/N), with strict sign classification. These analytic estimates apply for sufficiently large even N and every gamma>0. A standalone checker compares the Gram solve to the hat formula and verifies 74 finite diagnostics; those computations are supporting evidence, not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The full-grid theorems address a different Gram matrix; their positivity and higher-order asymptotic positivity do not imply the weight signs for the N-2 retained sites. Bartel et al. introduce subsampling but do not give this sharp two-erasure parameter threshold in the material inspected. Broad stability conditions for general kernels do not imply the quantified two-term asymptotic.

value.rationale: Deleting precisely the two nodes at zeros of a natural periodization density trades two observations for a sharp 7/3-fold higher allowable Korobov parameter before unconstrained optimal quadrature weights turn negative. This gives a quantitatively motivated stability design rule for the sampled lattice method, with sharp constant and next-order term, beyond a routine restatement of the standard kernel interpolant. It does not claim improved worst-case integration error or other erasure patterns.
